blindSummary:
This state/province operates parallel religious criminal law as one of twelve states whose religious courts have jurisdiction to try criminal cases for adherents of that faith. The religious penal code criminalises same-sex sexual acts between men and between women, extending beyond what the national statute covers. No trans-specific incident or religious-morality-corps enforcement appears for this state/province in the source dossier. The framework's capital-punishment provisions for some sexual offences are shared across the bloc.

The divergence from the national picture rests on the parallel criminal jurisdiction existing on statute and being operational rather than on documented enforcement: one sibling state's religious penal code was the first of the adoption wave and hosts the bloc's most active morality-corps force, and another sibling has that corps specifically named in the record; this state/province has no comparable documentation and stands at the bloc's generic legal baseline.
